children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures closed lower on Thursday  on a lack of bullish news and lingering hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough to ease disruptions to Black Sea grain exports, traders said.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) settled down 3-3/4 cents at $7.27 per bushel.
K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) ended down 5 cents at $7.94-1/2 a bushel and Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) fell 3-1/2 cents to finish at $7.52-1/2 a bushel.

In Europe, wheat traders said an AFP report, which cited a Turkish proposal sent to Russia and Ukraine for a truce on strikes against commercial shipping in the Black Sea, stirred hopes of military de-escalation in the Black Sea grain export region.

However, traders were cautious given that Turkey has already flagged such proposals, while a Russia-Ukraine deal to halt strikes on energy infrastructure announced by U.S. President Trump on Monday had little effect on the ground.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported net export sales of U.S. wheat in the week ended September 10 at 325,900 metric tons, in line with trade expectations for 150,000 to 500,000 tons.
The International Grains Council raised its 2026/27 world wheat crop outlook by 3 million tons to 820 million tons, driven by upward revisions for Australia and Ukraine.
The IGC report said, however, that global wheat flows were unusually slow due to disruptions to Black Sea exports.
